task.description: Write test/specs/REQ-029.md and add test cases to test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs (extend the existing file, matching REQ-028's established style) covering validate_node_attributes/1, validate_edge_conditions/1, and valid_cel_syntax?/1. Application-executable surface clearly exists (lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex extended with real logic) -- full test design procedure applies, no scope-skip.
acceptance_criteria: each of the 7 node types has at least one explicit test: HUMAN_TASK missing role, SERVICE_TASK missing endpoint, SERVICE_TASK invalid timeout (0 and >300000), TIMER missing/invalid duration, TIMER P0D explicitly accepted, and START/END/gateway types accepting no attributes
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edge with both a non-null condition and is_default: true is rejected
an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with two edges both marked is_default: true is rejected
isValidCelSyntax-equivalent rejects at least one structurally invalid expression and accepts at least one structurally valid one, with an explicit test noting it performs no evaluation
extra undeclared attributes on a node do not cause a violation, demonstrated by an explicit test

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-029.md and extended test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs (in place, matching the REQ-028 style) with 25 new ExUnit test cases across 12 describe blocks covering all 5 REQ-029 acceptance criteria: AC1 (14 cases + 2 composition tests) for all 7 node types incl. HUMAN_TASK missing role, SERVICE_TASK missing endpoint, SERVICE_TASK timeout 0/300001 invalid and 1/300000 boundary-valid, TIMER missing/malformed duration (7 malformed variants) and P0D/other valid durations, and START/END/EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY/PARALLEL_GATEWAY requiring nothing; AC2 (1 case) the default+condition co-firing rejection asserting both :unexpected_edge_condition and :default_with_condition fire; AC3 (3 cases) two- and three-default-edge rejection plus the one-default-is-legal happy path; AC4 (3 standalone cases + 1 wiring/integration case) valid_cel_syntax?/1 accept/reject examples plus an explicit no-evaluation demonstration and a check_cel_syntax/1 integration test; AC5 (1 case) extra undeclared attributes causing no violation. Every fixture was hand-traced against the actual merged lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex before being written, not guessed from the design doc alone -- one first-draft assertion (SERVICE_TASK attributes: nil expected only :missing_endpoint) was caught wrong by actually running the suite and corrected to the real two-code result ([:missing_endpoint, :invalid_timeout]), documented in the spec's 'Regression note'. Full file: mix test test/letflow/definitions/graph_test.exs -> 40 tests, 0 failures (15 pre-existing REQ-028 + 25 new REQ-029). mix format --check-formatted clean.
